- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect mean reversion toward recent highs.
- Model consistently underreacts to sentiment spikes; if sentiment jumps to 1.00, forecast should be adjusted upward by 2–5% for 3–5 days.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >7% from prior day) are common; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for 2–3 days.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts; if sentiment changes direction within 3 days, forecast should be revised within 1–2 days to align with sentiment trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if recent 18-day average is below 65.00.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to overfit short-term trends; smooth forecasts with 3-day moving average to reduce noise.
